historical_reviews.deepseek: Its generic all-NVMe output cannot identify which controllers occupy E1.S bays and does not test the required speed/width fields.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly demands E1.S-specific physical mapping and complete per-BDF link evidence while maintaining read-only scope.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code/source search found no earlier V3.1 record for this identity.
historical_reviews.v3_1: E1.S drives are front-serviceable bay devices whose Linux controller indices do not encode bay position. Acceptance therefore needs the platform backplane/bay routing map and controller serial-to-BDF correlation; otherwise an internal M.2 controller can be miscounted as an E1.S device and a missing bay can remain hidden.

original_test_intent: Verify the complete E1.S NVMe bay population, device identity and actual PCIe speed/width against the approved E1.S platform specification.
original_method: Authenticate the exact platform and backplane, collect all NVMe controllers/namespaces and block identity, map each expected E1.S bay through its controller serial and PCIe BDF, capture complete lspci capability/negotiated-link state, compare identity/capacity/transport/link fields with the E1.S recipe, and keep all operations read-only.
manual_activity: The storage/platform owner approves the E1.S bay/backplane-to-controller/BDF map, expected device/link matrix and treatment of optional or empty bays.
required_inputs: Expected model, serial policy, capacity and firmware if applicable
Expected PCIe generation and width per bay
Verified host-key SSH and secret-safe authentication
safety_requirements: Do not hot-remove or insert E1.S devices in this case
Do not infer bays from `/dev/nvmeX` indices
Exclude internal M.2 and other NVMe controllers from E1.S coverage by approved mapping
Never expose credentials or disable host verification
Do not reset, rescan, format, sanitize or manage namespaces
agent_execution_scope: Collect complete NVMe and block inventory
Map only approved E1.S controller serials to bays and BDFs
Capture complete per-BDF PCIe identity and negotiated link state
Compare all bay-level fields to the E1.S recipe
Report omissions or mismatches without changing storage
engineer_actions: Approve expected population and optional-bay policy
Distinguish E1.S from internal M.2 endpoints
Resolve missing, duplicate or downtrained bay evidence

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `lsblk` and `nvme list` provide generic NVMe inventory but do not identify E1.S bays or collect the source-required PCIe speed/width. Unsafe SSH also breaks target provenance.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Over verified SSH, collect complete block/NVMe controller and namespace inventory, then `lspci -s <approved-E1.S-BDF> -nn -vvv` for every mapped bay and compare identity plus LnkSta/LnkCap to the E1.S SPEC.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All E1.S bays, the lspci speed/width check and the 10-minute source estimate remain in scope.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a bay-keyed matrix joining backplane port, controller serial/model, namespace set, BDF, capacity, LnkCap and LnkSta, with non-E1.S NVMe endpoints explicitly excluded.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds backplane identity, bay-specific mapping, controller/namespace normalization and secure complete link collection.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: An all-NVMe list may look complete while the wrong E1.S bay is empty and an internal M.2 supplies the expected count; a generic lspci listing does not expose which bay is downtrained.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The data collection is read-only, but physical bay association cannot be inferred reliably from OS enumeration without the platform routing map.

project_override_considerations: Approve the current backplane/riser routing, expected populated and optional bays, shared-port or switch topology, permitted link states and whether controller firmware is a required information field under `All E1.S information`.
expected_evidence: SUT/BIOS/backplane identity, E1.S recipe revision and bay/controller/BDF map
Verified SSH provenance, tool versions and timestamps
Complete raw lsblk/NVMe controller/namespace inventory and per-E1.S-BDF lspci output
Bay-level comparison of model/serial/capacity/transport/firmware if required, LnkCap and LnkSta
Explicit exclusion of M.2/other NVMe endpoints, optional/mismatch disposition, preserved logs, no-mutation audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently target E1.S inventory and PCIe link properties. DeepSeek's generic E1.S/M.2 wording is not part of the authoritative source fields.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The E1.S target and read-only method are clear. A project map, SPEC and packages are identifiable execution inputs, so this remains REQUIRES.

review_improvement: Makes E1.S bay identity explicit and prevents a generic NVMe count or internal M.2 device from satisfying the front-bay coverage requirement.
independent_technical_reasoning: The same NVMe subsystem exposes E1.S and M.2 controllers uniformly, so software inventory alone cannot prove form factor or bay occupancy. A platform route from bay/backplane port to controller serial and BDF is the necessary identity anchor; negotiated link evidence must then be attached to that anchor to detect a missing or downtrained bay without performing any hot-plug or storage I/O.
